slides.title: Introduction to Modular Sass
slides.content:
# Modular Sass: Partials & Modules 📂

Writing all your styles in a single monolithic file is a recipe for chaos. Sass solves this through **Partials** and the modern **Module System** (`@use` and `@forward`).

## What You'll Learn:
- **Partials**: Creating modular snippet files with the `_` underscore convention
- **The Deprecation of `@import`**: Global namespace pollution and duplicated CSS
- **The `@use` Rule**: Encapsulated imports with clean namespaces
- **Aliasing Namespaces**: Using `as *` or `as custom`
- **File Forwarding with `@forward`**: Creating library entry points
- **Built-in Sass Modules**: `sass:math`, `sass:color`, `sass:map`, `sass:list`

slides.title: Creating Partials (_filename.scss)
slides.content:
# The Partials Convention: `_filename.scss` 🗂️

A **Partial** is a Sass file whose name begins with an underscore `_` (e.g., `_variables.scss`, `_buttons.scss`).

## What the Underscore Tells the Compiler

When the Sass compiler scans your directories:

- `main.scss` (no underscore) ➔ Compiled into standalone `dist/main.css`.
- `_buttons.scss` (with underscore) ➔ **NOT** compiled into a standalone CSS file. It is treated as an imported module piece!

## Example Project Structure (The 7-1 Pattern)

```
scss/
├── abstracts/
│   ├── _variables.scss
│   └── _functions.scss
├── components/
│   ├── _buttons.scss
│   └── _card.scss
└── main.scss   <-- Only this file compiles to main.css!
```

slides.title: Why @import is Deprecated
slides.content:
# Why `@import` Was Deprecated 🛑

For years, developers imported partials using `@import 'buttons'`. However, `@import` suffers from serious architectural flaws:

1. **Global Namespace Pollution**: Every variable, mixin, and function declared in any file existed in a single global scope. It was impossible to know where a variable originated!
2. **Name Collisions**: If two imported files declared `$primary-color`, one would silently overwrite the other.
3. **Code Duplication**: If 5 files each did `@import 'variables'`, mixins or rules were duplicated multiple times in compiled CSS.
4. **No Encapsulation**: Everything was public; private tokens could not be protected.

> ⚠️ **Official Deprecation:** The Sass core team officially deprecated `@import` in favor of `@use` and `@forward`.

Architectural Pattern: The 7-1 Architecture
slides.content:
# Enterprise Architecture: The 7-1 Pattern 🏛️

The **7-1 Pattern** is the industry standard directory structure for large Sass projects:

```
sass/
├── abstracts/     # Tools, helpers, variables, mixins, functions
├── base/          # Reset, typography, boilerplate styles
├── components/    # Reusable widgets: buttons, cards, sliders
├── layout/        # Major layout sections: header, footer, sidebar
├── pages/         # Page-specific styling: _home.scss, _contact.scss
├── themes/        # Multi-theme overrides: _dark.scss, _high-contrast.scss
├── vendors/       # Third-party CSS/libraries
└── main.scss      # Master entry point tying everything together
```

Each folder has an `_index.scss` file with `@forward` rules, making `main.scss` an elegant, one-page table of contents!

Summary: Partials & Modules
slides.content:
# Partials & Modules: Summary 📋

## Key Takeaways
- **Partials**: Named `_name.scss`; compiled only when loaded by a master file.
- **`@use`**: Replaces deprecated `@import`; provides strict file namespaces (`module.$var`).
- **`@forward`**: Packages and re-exports partials through `_index.scss` barrel files.
- **Private Members**: Prefix with `-` or `_` to keep tokens internal.
- **Built-in Modules**: Use `sass:math` (`math.div`), `sass:color` (`color.adjust`), `sass:map`, and `sass:string`.
- **7-1 Pattern**: Organizes enterprise code into clean functional folders.

Next: Master `@mixin` and `@function` for reusable code generation! ⚙️
